items.implementation: PostgreSQL advisory transaction lock accounts for existing documents plus durable reserved/stored/uncertain bytes before writing; pending count, user/global capacity, persistent per-user upload frequency, nginx ingress and MVC rate limits; disk free-space headroom includes outstanding reservations. Production MultipartFile ingestion and reconciliation use 8 KiB streaming buffers; write pass revalidates both size and digest against the pre-reservation hash.
counterexamples: Concurrent distinct uploads over user quota are rejected without new files
Pending-count, rate, global-byte and disk-low-water denial branches checked
A MultipartFile whose getBytes() throws can still be ingested; changing content between hash and write remains uncertain and is never silently published.
limits: Existing documents conservatively count as 20 MiB until their size is known; no original file is deleted
Single-host architecture remains the supported deployment boundary

items.implementation: Same owner + same SHA256 returns existing non-deleted document; in-flight same-hash reservation conflicts instead of writing a second file; other owners never receive another user's document.
counterexamples: Same content under another owner creates that owner's own document

items.implementation: Filesystem or database errors retain original file and reservation; stale inactive reservations are reconciled under the same global lock. Verified complete bytes recover metadata, missing files release reservation, corrupt files remain uncertain and charged.
counterexamples: Metadata transaction rollback retains the file and blocks duplicate retry until reconciliation
Successful commit with lost acknowledgment is not deleted or charged twice
Corrupt original is retained
limits: Uncertain files require administrator review; there is no destructive automatic cleanup

items.implementation: X-Auth-Mode: cookie explicitly selects same-origin HttpOnly SameSite=Strict session cookie. New browser login response contains no JWT. Mutations authenticated by cookie require a token derived from and bound to that session. Legacy Bearer API remains supported, and all credentials retain token_version revocation. Non-loopback cookies always carry Secure; the legacy false flag cannot downgrade them.
counterexamples: Missing/wrong CSRF returns 403
Logout invalidates old cookie and the same JWT presented as Bearer
BrowserSessionTest rejects non-loopback insecure cookies even when legacy false flag is set; loopback HTTP and HTTPS branches retained.
limits: Loopback HTTP development uses a non-Secure cookie; public deployment requires TLS
A confirmed XSS could still perform actions in the browser; HttpOnly is not an XSS cure
Legacy stored Bearer state can still be read for compatibility; new browser logins never write a JWT into Storage

items.implementation: Current-password-gated password change; password quality validation blocks common values and new passwords above bcrypt's 72-byte boundary; cryptographic one-time offline recovery code is stored only as SHA256. Recovery consumes the code, changes password, revokes all sessions and clears MFA for re-enrollment.
counterexamples: Recovery-code reuse returns 401
Old sessions fail after password change or recovery
limits: Existing password hashes preserve legacy bcrypt byte-truncation verification semantics
Without a pre-generated recovery code, lost-password identity verification needs an external operator process

items.implementation: Identity-hashed PostgreSQL attempt state applies progressive short blocks across clients and survives process restart; existing ingress IP limits remain.
counterexamples: After five failures correct credentials are temporarily blocked for that identity, another identity remains usable
items.repair: Initial Windows run exposed naive UTC timestamp interpreted in host timezone. Code now explicitly interprets schema timestamps as UTC; assertions preserved.

items.implementation: RFC6238 TOTP enrollment, expiring pending seed, explicit confirmation, one-use step enforcement, password-gated disable/rotation; AES-256-GCM encrypted seed with separate operator key. Enabled accounts must supply TOTP in both Cookie and Bearer login. ADMIN_MFA_REQUIRED=true removes admin roles until enrollment while keeping the security setup route usable. Enable/disable revoke old tokens.
counterexamples: Missing code fails for both login modes
Replayed code fails
Absent/mismatched storage key fails closed
Required-but-unenrolled administrator cannot access review APIs
items.repair: Pending-seed expiration uses UTC explicitly after Windows timezone regression was detected.
limits: Operator must generate ACCOUNT_SECURITY_ENCRYPTION_KEY as independent random 32-byte base64 and preserve it with private recovery configuration; no production default key exists
ADMIN_MFA_REQUIRED is opt-in to allow an existing administrator to enroll before enforcement

items.implementation: Nginx redacts API and frontend capability-token paths in access logs; share locations suppress request-bearing error logs, retain redacted status/request_id access evidence, and emit no-store/no-referrer. Java shared-trip responses also use no-store.
counterexamples: A token must not appear in captured access or error logs
limits: An external TLS reverse proxy or third-party collector requires its own capability-URL redaction; repository nginx cannot configure that external layer

items.implementation: TokenService maps DataAccessException to 503 AUTH_STORE_UNAVAILABLE, retaining 401 for malformed, forged, expired or revoked tokens. The security filter preserves the retryable 503 classification so the frontend's 401 logout handler is not activated.
counterexamples: A signed valid JWT with a failed user/revocation DAO must return 503, and becomes usable after the DAO recovers
Forged, expired and malformed tokens still return 401 before querying the failed store

external_gaps.reason: No user-approved email/SMS transport, sender identity, public callback domain or channel acceptance credentials supplied; offline recovery is locally verifiable.
Public HTTPS endpoint and upstream log pipeline are outside repository runtime; their TLS/cookie/log-redaction acceptance needs the actual deployment.

qa.main_question: 上传容量如何在并发、进程崩溃及数据库提交结果不确定时仍保持可核对？
qa.answer: 先在PostgreSQL事务锁下计算已有文件和所有未决预留，持久化预留后再写文件；文件写入和文档元数据完成阶段受同一锁保护。失败不推断事务一定回滚，不删文件，保留额度。管理员核对只处理过期且无本进程活跃写入的预留；完整哈希文件恢复入库，确实缺失释放额度，损坏文件保留待人工核查。测试分别注入元数据失败和提交后响应丢失。

followups.question: Cookie为什么还需要CSRF，Bearer兼容会不会绕过MFA？
followups.answer: Cookie会随浏览器自动发送，所以写操作要求与该会话JWT绑定的CSRF头。Bearer兼容只改变凭证传输，仍调用同一密码和TOTP登录校验；启用MFA会递增token_version，使启用前的所有旧凭证失效。已启用账号在两种模式下都必须提供未用过的验证码。

followups.question: 恢复码或MFA密钥丢失怎样处理，哪些内容还不能声称交付？
followups.answer: 恢复码是一次性高熵秘密，仅哈希落库；使用会重设密码、撤销旧会话并清除旧MFA。MFA存储密钥需要部署方随机生成并随私有配置备份，丢失或不匹配必须报错，不能免校验放行。邮件/SMS通道和公网TLS入口未提供，单独标记blocked_external；离线恢复、TOTP和Cookie链路可在隔离本机验证。
